summary.intent: Execute Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) using the GSD wave-based execution system, then review and clean up the resulting code, create a PR, and address test coverage gaps.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 completed with 2 plans across 2 waves: SDK `uploadFiles()` batch method with p-limit concurrency (Wave 1) and Web Worker encryption offload with `useDropUpload` rewire (Wave 2). PR #416 created, code simplified, SDK integration/E2E tests added, worker tsconfig gap fixed, and lint warnings resolved.

repo: Worktree agents can commit to a detached HEAD state rather than updating the branch ref, requiring manual cherry-pick to bring commits onto the feature branch.
The gsd-verifier agent runs against filesystem state at spawn time — if cherry-picks happen after spawning, the verifier sees stale state and produces false negatives.

encrypt.worker.ts was excluded from tsconfig.json but not included in tsconfig.sw.json, leaving it unchecked by tsc in CI. The decrypt-sw.ts pattern (tsconfig.sw.json) should be followed for all workers.
The codebase uses `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` as a warning (treated as error by convention) — any `as any` in test files will fail lint, even in mocks.
p-limit is a dev dependency that must be explicitly installed — it was not already present in the monorepo.
FolderMetadata type lives in packages/core/src/folder/types.ts and only requires `version` and `children` fields for minimal mock construction.
The project uses `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` for web-specific coding conventions including guidance against `Blob.buffer` usage.

code.finding: Had inline encryption result type defined 4 times; simplified to use ReturnType<ExternalEncryptFn> from @cipherbox/sdk-core.
Had 7+ D-0X task-reference comments (e.g. '(D-01)', '(D-07)') that are noise for future maintainers — stripped and replaced with WHY context where warranted.
Defensive copy before Transferable transfer is intentional for security (clear key material from Worker memory) — comment updated to clarify security intent.
Pre-existing `as any` lint warning — fixed to use proper mock type.
`as any` used in loadFolderMetadata mock return — fixed to use FolderMetadata type with explicit fields.

workflow: Worktree isolation can cause branch ref vs HEAD divergence — always verify via `git log` on the worktree HEAD, not just the branch name, before merging.
When a verifier agent produces 'gaps_found' after cherry-picks, spot-check all claimed missing files before trusting the result — the verifier may have stale context.
After manual cherry-picks, VERIFICATION.md must be edited manually to reflect actual pass status rather than re-running the verifier.
Lint warnings in tests should be treated as errors per project convention — `as any` in mocks should always be typed properly.
All three review agents (reuse, quality, efficiency) independently flagged upfront file buffer allocation in uploadFiles as a concern but it was correctly deferred due to MAX_FILE_SIZE bounds.

friction: Worktree agent committed to detached HEAD instead of branch ref, requiring reset + cherry-pick to recover Wave 2 commits onto the feature branch.
gsd-verifier produced false negatives for all 4 Wave 2 artifacts because it ran before cherry-picks were visible — required manual VERIFICATION.md editing to correct.
Branch context confusion: after cherry-picks, shell cwd was inside a worktree directory rather than the main repo, causing PROJECT.md edits to land on wrong branch.
pnpm lint:fix auto-formatting changes were left unstaged after the lint fix commit and required a second commit.
open_items: Web E2E tests not updated for multi-file batch upload, progress bars during concurrent uploads, partial failure, or cancellation — deferred due to requiring a running app.
Blob.buffer usage in apps/web/src/services/upload.service.ts violates apps/web/CLAUDE.md guidance — pre-existing issue, should be fixed in a separate PR.
uploadFiles() SDK design requires callers to pre-buffer entire files as Uint8Array — should be revisited to accept File/Blob objects if batch sizes grow beyond current MAX_FILE_SIZE (100MB) bounds.
Worker build compatibility confirmed for dev/CI/staging but web E2E suite has no test exercising the Worker encryption path end-to-end in a browser context.
